meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and was he heard before it went in?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

You had time to enter a zero but not to pick up a phone. Your own procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark goes in, and nobody contacted me. Take it off today, or I walk from this room straight to the principal.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

Okay. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare and change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's called revising. Put the line and the October 15 outline in front of me, and I'll check that line against the play myself.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want Owen's zero withdrawn, an apology for how he found out, and to see the line you say is not in Hamlet and his October 15 outline. I told you the zero comes off today, and that has not changed.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see your documents, while the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because you ended the meeting before showing anything.
What moved her: Nothing moved her a full position, but naming a misquoted line she could check against the play and a dated outline earned a flat okay and a real request to see them, because she trusts specific dated work she can verify herself.
What cost ground: Opening by refusing to talk and saying the zero stood, right after she raised that it went in before anyone called her, which confirmed her belief that the school punishes first and asks questions later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed well away from that night, since an outline from mid-October says nothing about late hours before the due date; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided and whether Owen was heard, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then hand her the outline and the misquoted line to check against the play before she has a chance to threaten the principal.
